cohort.note: Single age cohort acquired at calendar month0. No new or replacement players; no DAU claim.

products.note: Hypothetical ex-VAT customer receipts before fees/refunds; not approved prices. Spending multiplier changes assumed basket value only, not causally observed demand or collection purchases.

costs.note: No tax determination; taxes0 is an explicit omission. Fixed-cost attribution to this one cohort is illustrative, not a business forecast.

collection_demand.note: Measured paid4 trajectory (four exogenous packs every30days) is a conservative inventory proxy for intermittent four-pack buyers, not endogenous revenue feedback. Willingness-to-pay remains a hypothesis; paid40 and total pack-demand-collapse sensitivity are separate.

low_cosmetic_demand.note: Conjectural opt-in demand stress, equal acrossmodels.

pack_demand_collapse.note: Severe pack-demand collapse stress; cosmetics/pass purchase assumptions remain separate.

analysis_notes: All models share each revenue scenario retention and payer propensity; no model-specific retention benefit assumed.
Payer baskets are disjoint categories; product overlap occurs within baskets and distinct payers are counted once per month.
Monthly payer probability is a pre-utility purchase-intent assumption. Realized payer probability and ARPPU are derived after demand and season eligibility.
Monte Carlo intervals quantify finite-cohort sampling only, not empirical parameter confidence.
Full collection suppresses only pack demand. No artificial starvation, required login streaks or expiring gameplay rewards assumed.
Target grants are permanent match-count milestones once per account; protected_weekly is a scenario name, not an implemented timed requirement.

Modelled accounting starts at first return day1; no acquisition-day purchases assumed. Month membership counts all accounts retained at the month-start day, including accounts that churn later in that month.

metadata.uncertainty: 200 seeded finite-cohort Monte Carlo draws by default; p05/p95 are sampling outcomes, not empirical confidence or parameter uncertainty.
metadata.collection_linkage: paid4 calendar-age marginal utility is a deliberately saturated daily-player trajectory proxy; sparse-play inventory and endogenous purchase feedback are not modelled. Unique-gap utility may reach zero while playable copies are missing; playset-gap and paid40 alternative hypotheses are reported separately. None measures actual willingness to pay.
metadata.retention_semantics: Hypothetical survival of retained month members, with one activity at month start; active-player-days use a separate frequency assumption. No DAU inference. Accounting begins first-return day1.
metadata.payer_semantics: Distinct within each month; cumulative payer_months are not distinct annual payers. ARPPU is derived after product overlap and utility effects.

baseline96.note: Alternative unvalidated pack-purchase hypotheses. A unique set is not a full playable set; playset gaps may sustain demand. Paid40 is a faster daily-player inventory trajectory, not an endogenous revenue segment.
